reasoning: Shows two stacked checkmarks beside horizontal lines, universally understood as a checklist or to-do list. Because every item in a task manager is already a task, this icon is only useful when the task's actual object is a checklist, packing list, or set of acceptance criteria, rather than generic tasks beginning with 'check'.

pass1.ambiguity: Very similar to clipboard checklist icons or bulleted list icons; inside a to-do app it is self-referential UI chrome unless the task itself is specifically about making or reviewing a checklist.

distinguishing: Places the two checkmarks on the left and the horizontal text lines on the right (standard left-to-right checklist layout), making it virtually interchangeable in meaning with the version that puts checkmarks on the right.
